Insurance

Medical Insurance in Kenya

Medical insurance pays for treatment costs within the limits and rules of the plan you choose. Plans differ widely in what they cover, which hospitals you can use, and what they exclude. The best plan is the one that matches your health needs and budget, not simply the cheapest premium.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Inpatient treatment and hospitalisation
  • Outpatient consultations, tests and medication, on plans that include them
  • Optional benefits such as maternity, dental and optical, on some plans
  • Evacuation and other extensions on certain plans

Who needs it

  • Individuals and families
  • Employers arranging staff cover
  • Self-employed people and SMEs
  • People moving from a group scheme to personal cover

Common risks

Surprise exclusions

Pre-existing conditions, waiting periods and sub-limits can affect what is paid. Read these before you buy.

Limits that run out

An overall limit can be used up by a single serious illness. Check the limits for inpatient, outpatient and specific benefits.

Network restrictions

Plans may be tied to hospital networks and co-payment rules.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Medical underwriting can lead to loadings, exclusions or declines.
  • Waiting periods may apply to certain benefits.
  • Benefits and premiums depend on the insurer and plan.

What affects the premium

  • Age of each member
  • Inpatient and outpatient limits
  • Hospital network or region
  • Optional benefits
  • Medical history
  • Number of members

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Names, ages and dates of birth of members
  • Benefits wanted: inpatient, outpatient, maternity, dental, optical
  • Existing medical conditions to disclose
  • Preferred hospitals or regions
  • Current plan, if any

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Why do I need to disclose my medical history?

Insurers rely on accurate disclosure to price and accept cover. Non-disclosure can lead to a claim being declined. Tell us everything relevant and we will present it properly.

Individual or group cover?

Employers with enough staff can often arrange group cover, which may offer broader acceptance terms. Individuals usually buy personal cover. We guide you on what is available.
